title: 16-time convicted felon arrested for stealing thousands in lawn equipment in Polk County: sheriff - NewsBreak
text:
By Emi Darquea ,
8 hours ago
TAMPA, Fla. (WFLA) — A convicted felon is facing burglary charges in Polk County for stealing thousands of dollars’ worth of lawn equipment.
He is now facing 33 charges, including multiple drug possession charges.
Lakeland house cleaner accused of stealing around 12K worth of jewelry from elderly woman “He did some burglaries in Lakeland,” Sheriff Grady Judd said. “He did some burglaries in the unincorporated area of Lakeland. Our detectives, who are the very best, caught up with him. We serve search warrants. We arrested him.”
Judd said back on Feb. 9, Randy Whitfield snuck into Floralawn on Combee Road South and took around $14,000 worth of equipment. Authorities shared a video with us, where they say Whitfield was driving away after stealing the equipment in a white Ford truck.
Robert Averitt, owner of Floralawn, said he’s never seen anything like this.
“We’ve been, on in this location in Polk County for over 20 years, and we’ve not had this type of thing happen to us before,” Averitt told 8 On Your Side.
Averitt showed us the fence with barbed wire where he keeps his equipment and said, “You know, if you’re going to try to get past all this, that must mean you really want the weed eaters.”
According to law enforcement, this wasn’t the first time the suspect faced problems for similar charges. The Hillsborough County jail’s website said he was arrested back in January for multiple charges, including burglary.
“So he thought, heck, they’ve caught me over here in Hillsborough County,” Judd said. “I’ll go over to Polk County, and I’ll do some burglaries and some thefts. He did some burglaries in Lakeland. He did some burglaries in the unincorporated area of Lakeland. Our detectives, who are the very best, caught up with him. We served search warrants. We arrested him.”
Whitfield is currently at the Polk County jail, facing a bond of over $300,000 dollars.
“Keep an eye on this guy. If he shows up in your neighborhood, he’s stealing something, because that’s what he does for a living, that’s his job. He’s a professional criminal,” Sheriff Judd told NewsChannel8.
